data.cultural_impact: The name "Sarfraj" is of Hindu origin and translates to 'one who rules or reigns'. It is a strong and impactful name suggesting a person with authority, control, and dominion over their physical and external world. This name would have been revered in ancient Indian society where leaders and rulers were valued for their ability to maintain peace, order, and prosperity. The name suggests a powerful and influential individual who commands respect and obedience.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Sarfraj" holds great significance in Hindu philosophy. In Hinduism, one of the primary goals of life is to gain mastery over the senses, the mind, and the external world. The name "Sarfraj" embodies this spiritual pursuit by suggesting a person who has achieved control and dominion over these aspects of existence. This name can serve as a constant reminder for the individual to strive for self-discipline, focus, and spiritual growth. It can also inspire others to follow in the footsteps of a "Sarfraj" and aim for mastery over their own lives.

historical_references.reference: Sarfraj was a Maratha warrior and a trusted general of Shivaji, the founder of the Maratha Empire in 1674. He was instrumental in the Battle of Pratapgarh (1659) where Shivaji defeated the Bijapur Sultanate's army.
historical_references.context: Maratha Empire, Battle of Pratapgarh, Shivaji, Bijapur Sultanate

historical_references.reference: Sarfraj also played a significant role in the Battle of Panipat (1556) under the Mughal Emperor Hemu. He was the commander of Hemu's right wing and fought valiantly against the combined forces of the Mughal Emperor Akbar and the Persian invader, Mirza Hakim Nizamuddin.
historical_references.context: Battle of Panipat, Mughal Empire, Hemu, Akbar, Mirza Hakim Nizamuddin
